podcast.title: Experienced Jazz and R&B Drummer
podcast.body: Al Jackson was an older black musician who had honed his skills playing jazz and R&B throughout the 1950s. He had previously played with Booker T. Jones in Willie Mitchell's band. "Al Jackson, who liked Steinberg was an older black man, who had cut his teeth playing jazz and R&B throughout the 50s."

podcast.title: First Full-Time Musician at Stax
podcast.body: Stax eventually agreed to pay Al Jackson a salary instead of one-off session fees, making him the first musician employed by the label as a full-time player. This marked a significant commitment from the label to its house band. "Eventually, stacks agreed to take him on an assallery, rather than just paying him one off session fees, and so he became the first musician employed by stacks as a full-time player."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Reluctance to Play Sessions
podcast.body: Jackson initially resisted playing sessions at Stax, believing they would be less lucrative than his regular gigging with Willie Mitchell's band. He wanted to avoid wasting his time on potentially unrewarding work. "Jackson was making money from gigging, and didn't want to waste his time playing sessions, which he thought would not be as lucrative as his regular gigs with Willie Mitchell."
